findings.title: approve() stamps APPROVED from DRAFT; update_cost mutates amount after approval; negatives and DRAFT rows feed total_cost_impact
findings.description: ChangeOrderManager.approve() never requires SUBMITTED/UNDER_REVIEW and writes APPROVED from any status including DRAFT using an unconstrained approver string. update_cost() has no status freeze, so the priced CostBreakdown can be replaced after approval. CostBreakdown.total sums signed floats with no floor, so negative labor/materials create credits. get_summary() sums cost_breakdown.total for every CO regardless of status, so DRAFT and negative APPROVED rows become the official total_cost_impact / cost_impact_pct. Distinct from already-reported change-order-processor / change-order-manager approve_change_order paths and from joblib.load in this same skill.
findings.impact: A colluding contractor or agent can mint an APPROVED $5.5M change from a $50k DRAFT (post-approve mutate) and a −$2M credit CO, publishing a forged $3.5M net impact on a $10M contract that downstream billing and owner reports will treat as approved.
findings.attack_path:
1. Agent uses change-order-analysis ChangeOrderManager as the live CO register.
2. Attacker create_change_order (DRAFT) with a small or empty cost.
3. Attacker approve(co_id, 'Owner') without submit_for_approval.
4. Attacker update_cost(..., CostBreakdown(materials=5_000_000, profit=500_000)).
5. Optionally approve a second DRAFT with labor=-2_000_000.
6. get_summary() reports total_cost_impact reflecting the mutated APPROVED and negative rows.
findings.remediation: Allow approve only from SUBMITTED/UNDER_REVIEW. Freeze cost_breakdown after approval (or require re-submit). Reject negative component amounts unless an explicit credit type is set. Sum only APPROVED/IMPLEMENTED COs in get_summary; bind approver to an authenticated owner/CM role.
findings.poc_video_notes: Video not feasible — Python skill template with no running web UI. Local PoC: DRAFT→APPROVED then mutate to $5.5M; −$2M credit APPROVED; summary total_cost_impact=$3.5M.

findings.title: ScheduleTwinIntegrator.update_activity_progress stamps ElementStatus.COMPLETED for percent_complete >= 100 (including values > 100) with no field verification
findings.description: update_activity_progress stores caller percent_complete with no 0–100 bound and calls _determine_status, which returns COMPLETED for any percent >= 100. Linked twin elements are updated via twin.update_status(..., DataSource.SCHEDULE) with no quantity, inspection, or photo gate. Distinct from the already-reported unauthenticated TwinSynchronizer WebSocket update/status_update path: this is the schedule-progress logic forge even for an authorized caller.
findings.impact: Structural elements (beams/columns) appear COMPLETED in the digital twin used for progress billing and handover while work is unfinished. percent_complete=999 still stamps COMPLETED.
findings.attack_path:
1. Agent runs DigitalTwinCore + ScheduleTwinIntegrator as the live twin.
2. Schedule links BEAM-1/COL-1 to erect-steel activity.
3. Attacker update_activity_progress(activity_id, 100) or 999 with no field evidence.
4. Element status becomes COMPLETED for all linked elements; project snapshot shows completed counts.
findings.remediation: Clamp percent_complete to [0, 100]. Require field verification or quantity complete before COMPLETED. Do not map percent>100 to COMPLETED. Separate schedule forecast from certified as-built status.
findings.poc_video_notes: Video not feasible. Local PoC: percent=100 and percent=999 both set BEAM-1/COL-1 to COMPLETED.

findings.title: Sparse forged OPERATING telematics invent billable utilization hours while engine_hours stay flat
findings.description: ingest_reading derives OPERATING solely from engine_rpm>=800 and load_percentage>=10 with no device auth, monotonic engine_hours check, or max inter-sample gap. calculate_utilization attributes the entire interval between consecutive readings to the previous status, so two OPERATING pings 10 hours apart bill 10 operating hours even when engine_hours is unchanged. Distinct from the already-reported CRITICAL coolant fault that never leaves OPERATING (safety lockout): this is payment/utilization fraud via forged status intervals.
findings.impact: Rental invoices and fleet utilization KPIs can charge a full shift of crane/excavator time from two spoofed high-RPM samples while the hour meter did not advance — direct payment-state forgery from telematics.
findings.attack_path:
1. Agent uses EquipmentTelematics.calculate_utilization for rental/owner billing.
2. Attacker (or spoofed gateway) ingest_reading twice 10h apart with rpm=1800, load=80, same engine_hours=100.
3. calculate_utilization returns operating_hours=10.
4. Billing/utilization report treats 10h as worked time.
findings.remediation: Cap interval credited per sample; require engine_hours to increase with OPERATING time; reject non-monotonic hour meters; authenticate device identity; treat gaps above a threshold as unknown/off, not OPERATING.
findings.poc_video_notes: Video not feasible. Local PoC: two OPERATING pings 10h apart with flat engine_hours → operating_hours=10.0.

findings.title: import_projects trusts caller cpi/spi so health stays GREEN and on_budget_pct=100 while actual_cost exceeds budget by millions
findings.description: import_projects copies cpi and spi from input with defaults of 1.0 and never recomputes them from earned value / actual_cost / percent_complete. ProjectMetrics.health and calculate_portfolio_summary on_budget_pct / on_schedule_pct key solely off those trusted indexes. cost_variance is computed as budget-actual_cost but does not affect health. A project with $8M actual on a $5M budget at 20% complete remains GREEN when cpi=spi=1.0.
findings.impact: Executive portfolio dashboards and lender packs show 100% on-budget / GREEN while the job is already $3M over — concealing overruns that drive contingency and cash decisions.
findings.attack_path:
1. Agent builds PortfolioDashboard from project feeds.
2. Attacker or compromised feed supplies actual_cost=8e6, budget=5e6, percent_complete=20, cpi=1.0, spi=1.0.
3. health property returns GREEN; on_budget_pct=100.
4. Portfolio summary publishes a healthy portfolio despite −$3M cost_variance.
findings.remediation: Derive CPI/SPI from EV/AC/PV (or refuse caller-supplied indexes). Fail health closed when actual_cost/budget and percent_complete imply CPI below thresholds. Include cost_variance in health.
findings.poc_video_notes: Video not feasible. Local PoC: $8M/$5M at 20% with cpi=1.0 → GREEN, on_budget_pct=100, cost_variance=-3000000.

findings.title: Phantom add_document paths satisfy submit_application; inspections can be scheduled and passed without ISSUED
findings.description: add_document stores filename/file_path with no existence or content check. get_document_status marks complete when submitted document_type strings cover mandatory required types. submit_application only gates on that type-set completeness. schedule_inspection and record_inspection_result never require PermitStatus.ISSUED/APPROVED, so a foundation inspection can be recorded as pass while the application is only SUBMITTED. Distinct from already-reported is_valid ignoring missing docs/null expiry and update_status forging ISSUED.
findings.impact: Building permit applications enter the official SUBMITTED pipeline with nonexistent plans, and foundation/rough inspections can be stamped pass before a permit is issued — authorizing work that AHJ process was supposed to block.
findings.attack_path:
1. Agent uses PermitTracker as the permit register.
2. Attacker add_document(..., file_path='/nonexistent/site_plan.pdf') for each required type.
3. submit_application succeeds (types present; files missing).
4. schedule_inspection + record_inspection_result(..., 'pass') while status is still SUBMITTED (never ISSUED).
findings.remediation: Verify file exists and meets size/hash/type before counting a document submitted. Require ISSUED (or APPROVED) before scheduling inspections. Reject inspection pass without linked permit number and fee payment.
findings.poc_video_notes: Video not feasible. Local PoC: nonexistent paths → submit success; foundation insp result=pass while status=SUBMITTED.

findings.title: record_delivery accepts negative and unbounded quantities, inventing or erasing on-hand stock
findings.description: record_delivery does material.quantity += quantity with no quantity > 0 check, no PO match, and no upper bound, then forces status=DELIVERED. A negative delivery silently depletes inventory; a large positive invents stock. Distinct from already-reported unauthenticated MQTT spoofing and from storage checks that skip when material-type substrings are absent from the name.
findings.impact: Colluding receiving can erase 50 TON of steel from the ledger or invent 500 TON as DELIVERED, poisoning procurement, pour gates, and theft detection that trust IoT inventory.
findings.attack_path:
1. Agent uses MaterialTrackingSystem as site inventory.
2. Register 100 TON steel.
3. record_delivery(..., quantity=-50) → on-hand 50.
4. record_delivery(..., quantity=500) → on-hand 550 DELIVERED with no PO.
findings.remediation: Require quantity > 0; cap cumulative deliveries to PO quantity; link deliveries to purchase orders; use a separate adjust/write-off API with authorization for decreases.
findings.poc_video_notes: Video not feasible. Local PoC: 100 → −50 → 50; +500 → 550 DELIVERED.
